slides.headline: A comic-style investigation into a scam that traps Indians by phone just won a Pulitzer Prize.
Anand RK and Suparna Sharma won the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Illustrated Reporting and Commentary
slides.body: Mumbai-based illustrator Anand RK and Delhi-based journalist Suparna Sharma, working with Bloomberg's Natalie Obiko Pearson, won for 'trAPPed' - a graphic investigation into India's 'digital arrest' scam phenomenon, published by Bloomberg.

slides.headline: The story followed a neurologist held under fake 'digital arrest' by a phone scam.
slides.body: Using illustration alongside reporting, the project traced how scammers impersonate law enforcement over video calls to psychologically trap victims - a growing global problem the Pulitzer board cited for using visuals and words together to make it visible.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat benefits when Indian storytellers win the world's top journalism prize for exposing a uniquely Indian problem.
slides.body: An Indian illustrator and an Indian journalist took a scam that preys on Indians specifically and turned it into internationally recognized, prize-winning work.
